title: Reflective or formative measurement
summary: Whether indicators reflect a construct or form it is a theoretical decision about the construct, made before estimation and never because one specification gives better statistics.

body.text: In [[reflective-measurement]] the construct causes its indicators: the items are interchangeable manifestations, they should correlate highly, and dropping one does not change what is measured. In [[formative-measurement]] the indicators make up the construct: they can be uncorrelated, and dropping one changes the construct's meaning (Jarvis et al. 2003; Diamantopoulos & Winklhofer 2001).

items: Does a change in the construct cause changes in all items (reflective), or do changes in an item change the construct (formative)?
Are the items interchangeable, sharing one theme?
Must the items covary? If one rises, should the others?
Do the items share the same antecedents and consequences?

body.caption: Flip a small block between reflective (Mode A) and formative (Mode B) and watch which quality criteria apply.

body.text: The starter below has an index F whose four indicators were designed as separate components (they correlate only about .25). Declare F reflective and run: Cronbach's α is about .52 and the AVE about .41, so F seems to "fail". Those criteria assume a common factor, which F never was. The opposite error, declaring a reflective scale formative, hides genuine reliability problems and changes what the construct means (Jarvis et al. 2003).
body.title: Try a wrong model: misspecified measurement

mistake.title: Choosing formative because reflective criteria failed
mistake.text: Switching a block to formative when α or AVE look poor is a misuse: the specification must follow from the construct definition. Low reliability of a reflective scale is a measurement problem to report and fix, not a reason to relabel it.

tryIt.task: Run PLS-SEM on this model, then open construct F, change its measurement to reflective and run again. Compare α and AVE of F, and the F → Y path, between the two runs. Change F back afterwards.

checks.question: Which block is most plausibly formative?

options.text: Socio-economic status measured by income, education and occupational prestige.
options.feedback: Correct. The components define status, and a rise in income does not have to come with a rise in education.

options.text: Loyalty measured by "I would recommend…", "I will buy again…" and "I will stay with…".
options.feedback: These items express the same underlying disposition and should move together: reflective.

options.text: Anxiety measured by four items such as "I feel tense" and "I feel worried".
options.feedback: A state of anxiety plausibly causes all four feelings; the items are interchangeable manifestations.

checks.explanation: Formative indicators define the construct and need not correlate.

checks.question: You declare the index F reflective and obtain α = .52. What is the right conclusion?

options.text: α is the wrong criterion for an index; keep F as composite-formative and assess it with weights, indicator collinearity and content validity.
options.feedback: Correct. α measures internal consistency of interchangeable items, which an index does not need.
Deleting components of an index changes what it measures, and chasing α optimises a criterion that does not apply.

options.text: Report F as unreliable and drop it from the model.
options.feedback: F is not unreliable in any meaningful sense; it was simply misspecified as a common factor.

checks.explanation: Quality criteria follow the measurement model, not the other way round.
